recipes.name: Rich and Creamy Beef Stroganoff
ingredients_raw: 2 (2 pound) beef chuck roast, cut into 1/2-inch thick strips
1 teaspoon salt, or more to taste
0.5 teaspoon ground black pepper, or more to taste

steps.text: Place beef into a large bowl. Stir in red wine, salt, and black pepper. Marinate for 10 minutes, then remove beef and pat dry with a paper towel. Reserve remaining marinade.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in beef; cook and stir until browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer beef to a plate, then drain any remaining grease from the skillet.

Melt 2 tablespoons butter in the skillet over medium heat. Stir in onion, garlic, and a pinch of salt. Cook and stir until onion is soft and translucent, 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer onion mixture to the plate with beef; set aside.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add mushrooms; cook and stir until tender, about 10 minutes. Transfer mushrooms to a bowl; set aside.

Melt 1/4 cup butter in the skillet over medium heat. Whisk in flour; cook and stir until flour no longer tastes raw, about 4 minutes. Slowly whisk in beef stock. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly, then reduce heat to medium-low.

Pour in reserved marinade, Worcestershire sauce, red pepper flakes, and mustard, then add beef and onion mixture. Cover and simmer until meat is tender, about 1 hour. Season with salt and black pepper.
Stir in mushrooms, cream cheese, and sour cream about 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Rich and Creamy Beef Stroganoff
raw_recipe.description: This beef stroganoff recipe with sour cream and cream cheese is a cozy dish of tender beef and mushrooms in a thick gravy seasoned with red pepper.

video.description: Enjoy the wonderful richness of stroganoff in this simple preparation. Marinate chunks of beef chuck roast in red wine, salt and black pepper. Cook the beef until browned and set aside while you melt butter in the same pan and cook onion, garlic and salt; set those aside, cook mushrooms and set them aside, too. Next create a roux of butter, flour and beef stock. Add reserved red wine marinade, Worcestershire sauce, prepared mustard and red pepper flakes. Add back all the veggies and beef and simmer until meat is tender. Just before you serve, preferably over egg noodles, stir in sour cream and cream cheese!

review.reviewBody: I used a cheap cut of meat and half the amount called for (beef stew meat--hey, on a tight food budget!) and only a pound which meant a) I had to simmer my meat just a little longer and b) I doubled the mushrooms so I could fake the actual amount of meat I used. I used dijon mustard and I added a teaspoon each of dried basil and dried oregano. I did NOT add the extra salt as there was plenty in the beef broth I used. I served this with buttered egg noodles and roasted broccoli. Everyone loved it. There's just enough for someone to re-warm for lunch tomorrow. Very good.

BEST stroganoff recipe I have tried and I have tried many over the years. I simmer in the crockpot for several hours instead of stove top. I saute mushrooms with garlic prior to adding the cream cheese and sour cream. As one other commenter stated, I add 1 tsp of oregano and 1 tsp of basil. This is a hit every time I make this for family and friends.

Love this recipe... it reminds me of my childhood in the 1970s. We don't eat meat, so I subbed in 2 lbs of Beyond Meat ground "beef" and use no-chicken Better Than Bouillon to make the broth. I cook the onions, mushrooms and garlic together and add in the Beyond ground as the onions start to soften. I never remove anything from the pan... I just do the sauce right on top of everything (easy peasy). We LOVE this dish and my daughter asks for the "creamy hamburger pasta" now pretty often. It's become one of our go-to comfort dishes. I especially like this recipe as it does NOT use cream of mushroom soup, which I don't care for and a lot of stroganoff recipes call for.

It was excellent! Didn’t use mushrooms because I made it for guests who don’t like them. It was still great! I used beef tenderloin and saved the juice from the meat after browning. I added it to the leftover marinade and then added 1/2 cup to the sauce. It gave it a rich flavor. I didn’t use red pepper flakes, but added a dash of cayenne. I served it over homemade egg noodles. Yummy!
Didn’t use pepper flakes this time. Much better. Cut the onions up tinier, too. Marinated the meat for 2-3 hours like others. Much more tender.

Absolutely fantastic. Instead of the simmering in a pan, I put in a slow cooker—about 2 1/2 hours—and it really came together in the last 45 minutes. Used white wine. Added cream cheese at very end and just a couple of teaspoonfuls of sour cream—don’t think it needs much, if any, and it’s got such exquisite flavours already

Absolutely love this recipe I added way more onion after caramelizing them and I added more mushrooms also adding fresh mushrooms towards the end to give it some texture turned out fabulous. Beats cream of mushroom recipes any day.

I cannot begin to tell you how many times I've eaten Beef Stroganov. Yesterday I figured I'd try a new recipe, and this was without a doubt the most DELICIOUS I've ever eaten! I did cheat ever so slightly and cooked the mushrooms longer than prescribed, then adding some red white, reducing along with the onions and garlic. I also added some scallions, fresh chopped parsley, parmesan cheese and heavy whipping cream. This recipe is amazing - thanks for posting!!!
Delish! Only change was that I slow roasted the beef in a broth and mushrooms and wine first due to it being a cheaper cut (stew beef) to tenderize. Otherwise followed the rest! Very good!

It's good. It's a flavorful sauce that isn't "cream of mushroom" based. I put the slices of meat in a bowl with 8oz of red wine in the refrigerator starting in the morning and it marinated there all day, not just ten minutes. Like many others, I cut the red pepper flakes in half to 1tsp. It still has a touch of heat. This is a stroganoff, not a thai curry or something. I ended up using nearly 2 tsp of salt. Salt is obviously an intensely personal preference. And instead of the mix of cream cheese and sour cream called for, I used one 8oz tub of sour cream, since otherwise, I was going to have to buy both a tub of sour cream and a block of cream cheese, then have more than half of each of them leftover, that I'd have to put into some other dish. With two pounds of meat, this recipe makes a huge pot of food. For just two of us, we are going to get three dinners out of it, plus some lunch leftovers.

Very creamy and rich, delicious. A definite recipe to make again!

A few tweaks, I added more beef stock as it simmered so as not to dry out. Added 16 oz container of mushrooms sliced thin, 1 cup not enough. Watch the red pepper flakes, I only added 1 tsp and I thought perfect but other family members found too hot. So adjust the heat index for your family.

I made this using a 2.35 lb chuck roast and it was delicious. My husband and son both raved about it. I did add a little Kitchen Bouquet at the end to make it have a little more of a "beef color". It gave it a richer appearance without affecting the taste. Also added extra sauteed Bella mushrooms because we love them. I will definitely make again and I am really particular so that says a lot!!
The taste of all the flavors comes out in this dish. Enjoyed over Angel hair pasta. Made with healthier choices. Light, reduced fat, lower sodium and protein plus pasta.
Loved it!

This was the best beef stroganoff recipe I've found to date. I agree with others that 2 tsp of red pepper flakes was too much. While I followed the recipe exactly, I'll try marinating longer and using a slow cooker for the meat.
Used chicken stock instead of beef stock as that is what I had on hand. I forgot about step 7 but it still turned out great.

This was a really good recipe. I followed it exactly. first, it could use some herbs. I also would use a little less red pepper flakes. The meat was a little tough, but that was my fault. Should’ve cooked it longer. I rated it four stars because of the tweaks it needed. I will try again.

I made this recipe . I also made some tweaks. I added garlic. I did not as much butter. After Browning the beef, I let juices cook to nothing and added onions and garlic, let cook for three to four minutes and added flour then cream of mushroom soup, and then beef broth. I did not use red pepper flakes without removing anything from the pan.
Love it!!!
I had to make some major adjustments because I used my ninja crockpot but I got it I will say you need more than 1 cup of mushrooms happy cooking peeps!
